findings.title: [P2] Restrict login redirects to trusted same-origin targets
findings.body: When `returnUrl` comes from a login parameter, an absolute or protocol-relative attacker URL redirects authenticated users off-site. Validate the target and permit only trusted same-origin paths before calling `location.assign`.

findings.title: [P2] Do not log issued authentication tokens
findings.body: Whenever `recordIssuedToken` is called, it sends the live credential verbatim to `console.log` through `audit`. Retained browser or server logs can therefore expose replayable tokens to operators, support personnel, or telemetry systems. Record only non-sensitive metadata.

findings.title: [P1] Never send issued authentication tokens to the audit logger
findings.body:
Calling `recordIssuedToken` with a live bearer/session token writes the credential verbatim to browser consoles or collected server logs. Anyone with log access can replay the token until it expires.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restrict post-login redirects to trusted same-origin paths
findings.body:
If `returnUrl` is derived from a login query parameter, values such as `https://attacker.example` or `//attacker.example` send authenticated users to an attacker-controlled site. The previous implementation always navigated to `/dashboard`.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Validate and restrict the post-login redirect target
findings.body:
Any caller-controlled `returnUrl`, such as `https://attacker.example/phish` or potentially a `javascript:` URL where permitted, is passed directly to `location.assign`. An attacker who controls the login return parameter can redirect authenticated users off-site and facilitate phishing or script execution.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Stop writing issued tokens to logs
findings.body:
Every token passed to `recordIssuedToken` is emitted verbatim through `console.log`. When console output is retained, forwarded to telemetry, or accessible by support/operators, anyone with that access can recover still-valid bearer tokens and impersonate users.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
